Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National ‘If a mother’s tears could bring back a child’ – Javits’ mother breaks down during tribute Source : Kenneth Awotwe Darko 20 November 2026 6:52pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The mother of 15-year-old Badu Nkansah Frimpong, popularly known as Javits, broke down in tears during the reading of her tribute at his funeral in the Bronx, New York, as she struggled to come to terms with the loss of her only child.
The tribute, which was read on her behalf at the funeral on Friday, November 20, recounted her pain over the death of the son she had carried, nurtured and prayed for.
Standing beside the reader, Javits’ mother, Doris, became visibly emotional and broke down at the end of the reading.
In the message, she described Javits as her only son, her only child and her greatest blessing, saying that although distance separated them when he travelled to the United States to live with his father, their emotional bond remained strong.
She recalled their conversations and the dreams he shared with her, particularly his ambition to study hard, become a doctor and one day return to Ghana to take care of her and help less privileged people in their community.
“You told me that you wanted to study hard, become a doctor and return one day to take good care of me and help the less privileged in our community in Ghana,” the tribute read.
She said those words had become the foundation of her hopes and daily prayers, adding that she had imagined the day she would proudly call him “Doctor”.

The mother said she had looked forward to watching her son fulfil his ambitions and growing old with the comfort of knowing that he had achieved his dreams.
But his death, she said, had abruptly ended a future they had imagined together.
“My son, what hurts most is not just that you are gone, but everything you were yet to become. Your dreams, your laughter, your kindness and the beautiful future we imagined together have all been taken away,” she said.
In one of the most emotional passages, she expressed the depth of a mother's grief over the loss.
“If a mother’s tears could bring back a child, I would have cried you back into my arms. If love could defeat death, you would still be here,” the tribute read.
She ended by assuring her son that he would remain in her heart and that she would carry his dreams and memories for the rest of her life.
“Sleep well, my only son. My heart has lost its greatest treasure,” she said.
Javits was born on April 29, 2011, and moved from Ghana to the United States in 2025 to join his father and pursue his education. He aspired to become a doctor and serve in the United States military.
He was fatally shot in the Bronx on October 29, 2026, aged 15.
